answer_1.quote: After collecting relevant cases and reasons, this step leverages an LLM to summarize these past experiences and generate an interpretation of the vague concept.

answer_2.quote: For the classification task, we use Accuracy (Acc.), Macro Precision (Ma-P), Macro Recall (Ma-R), and Macro F1 (Ma-F) as the evaluation metrics. ... For the reason generation task, we use an LLMbased evaluator to evaluate the consistency between the generated reason r and the gold reason r from the court view.

answer_4.quote: We recruited 2 legal experts who have passed China's Unified Legal Profession Examination to assess the legal concept interpretations generated by Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct.
answer_4.guideline: They collaboratively establish five evaluation criteria and score the interpretations: (1) Accuracy (Acc.), (2) Informativeness (Info.), (3) Normativity (Norm.), (4) Comprehensiveness (Comp.), (5) Readability (Read.). We use a 10-point Likert scale, where 1 represents 'very poor' and 10 represents 'very good'.
